headline: Failed House bill would have delayed tax deadlines for Americans held hostage or wrongly detained abroad and ended tax exemptions for terrorist-supporting groups.
what_it_does: The bill would have pushed back certain tax filing deadlines for U.S. nationals who are held hostage abroad or unlawfully or wrongfully detained abroad, and for their spouses. It would also have allowed refunds and cancellation of tax penalties and fines paid by these individuals and their spouses or dependents. Separately, it would have ended the tax-exempt status of organizations found to support terrorism. The House voted it down on November 12, 2024.

who_it_affects.group: U.S. nationals held hostage or wrongfully detained abroad
who_it_affects.how: They would have gotten more time to file certain taxes and could have had tax penalties and fines refunded or canceled.

who_it_affects.group: Spouses and dependents of hostages and detained Americans
who_it_affects.how: Spouses would have received delayed filing deadlines, and spouses or dependents could have had related tax penalties and fines refunded or canceled.

who_it_affects.group: Tax-exempt organizations deemed to support terrorism
who_it_affects.how: They would have lost their tax-exempt status.
